newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed, 2nd Board at all-time high.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed, 2nd Board at all-time high.

text.p: Shares ended mixed with blue chips succumbing to profit taking, and second board surging to an all-time high.
Traders said investors who had expected quick handouts from the 1997 Budget presented last Friday were disappointed.
"There was some disappointment that there were no fast handouts like tax-cuts," said a foreign brokerage salesman. "It's the usual case of expectations running ahead of facts."
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index fell 10.86 points to 1,162.09. The Second Board index was up 5.74 to 637.10, against the Oct 21 all-time high of 635.84.

"Everyone's going for the seven to eight ringgit (second board) stocks," said a Mayban Securities trader. He said the secondaries are likely to continue rising this week after breaking a new high on heavy volumes today.
Second boarders Setegap, General Lumber, Trenergy and UCM were among laggard second boarders which were pushed up between 40 cents and 2.40 ringgit.
Another second board issue, Dataprep, jumped 1.60 to 18.50 on a national budget that is viewed as friendly to high-techonology companies and continuing speculation over new high-tech projects.
